subject: Post-call: Connective.ai trial scope & ops next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@connective.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@connective.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Connective.ai trial scope & ops next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment overall. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the trial/POC planning.

Call highlights:
- Goal: validate extract-and-normalize pipeline for customer support transcripts and achieve parity with current rule-based latency/throughput while improving quality of entity extraction.
- Primary KPIs: 95th-pct latency <= 300ms per request (95th token latency for streaming), sustained throughput target 120 reqs/min under realistic fanout, cost target <$0.004 per 1k tokens for inference pathway, and label-level precision/recall > 0.88 on the provided sample set.
- Data: Samir will share a de-identified 5k-sample set (schema attached as trial-data-sample.csv).

Proposed 3-week ops sprint (tentative):
Week 0 (this week) — intake & baseline:
  - Share data sample (Samir) and upload to secure trial bucket (Connective will provide temporary access).
  - Redwood: run smoke benchmark on hosted preview model and return baseline latency/cost per token.
Week 1 — tuning & instrumentation:
  - Redwood to provide model profile and recommended batching/quantization settings for their workload.
  - Instrumentation: we’ll push tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdown to your Workspace.
Week 2 — acceptance & readout:
  - Run gated acceptance tests on 1k holdout sample; compute precision/recall, 95th-pct latency, throughput sweeps.
  - Final readout + suggested rollout plan (canary split and rollback thresholds).

Owners (first-pass):
- Redwood ops: Rafael Mendes (trial lead), Ben Carter (performance tuning, infra).
- Customer ops: Samir Patel (data access, evaluation sign-off), Alyssa Chen (product use-cases).
- CS handoff: Monica Patel (onboarding & runbook).

Attachments: trial-data-sample.csv (schema), ops-checklist.xlsx (ops task list stub).

Next steps: Samir to post data by EOD Mon 9/20; Redwood to run baseline tests by Tue 9/21 and share results. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148
From: Samir Patel <samir@connective.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@connective.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Connective.ai trial scope & ops next steps

Thanks Rafael — that summary looks right to me. I’ve pulled a 5k de-identified sample and uploaded the CSV to our secure S3 share; link is internal to Connective (I’ll send access to your service account).

Couple of clarifications:
- For cost, the target we care about is cost-per-conversation (avg ~250 tokens) rather than per-1k tokens; equivalently we’d like the end-to-end inference cost to be under $0.10/conversation during the trial. Can you translate your per-token number to that baseline in the readback?
- We’ll need evidence of KV-cache behavior for sessionized conversations — if your runtime can provide per-session cache hit rates that’d help our evaluation.

Timeline works for us; I’ll grant the bucket access and notify when it’s available (aiming EOD Mon PST).

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Connective.ai
samir@connective.ai
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Connective.ai trial scope & ops next steps

Forwarding Samir’s notes — he’s provided the sample and asked for two clarifications (cost per conversation and KV-cache hit evidence). See my inline thoughts below.

> On Sat, 19 Sep 2026 at 16:08:00 -0700, Samir Patel <samir@connective.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks Rafael — that summary looks right to me. I’ve pulled a 5k de-identified sample and uploaded the CSV to our secure S3 share; link is internal to Connective (I’ll send access to your service account).
> > 
> > Couple of clarifications:
> > - For cost, the target we care about is cost-per-conversation (avg ~250 tokens) rather than per-1k tokens; equivalently we’d like the end-to-end inference cost to be under $0.10/conversation during the trial. Can you translate your per-token number to that baseline in the readback?
> > - We’ll need evidence of KV-cache behavior for sessionized conversations — if your runtime can provide per-session cache hit rates that’d help our evaluation.
> 
My notes:
- Cost translation is straightforward — we’ll run baseline runs on the 250-token normalized conversation and report both per-1k-token and per-conversation numbers. We should include best/worst-case with different batching sizes.
- KV cache: need to confirm sessionization approach with infra; Ben can confirm whether our tracing hooks already record per-session cache hits or if we need an ad-hoc metric.

Action items for internal ops:
- Ben: verify whether the preview runtime produces per-session cache hit metrics and draft a plan for exposing that in the instrumentation by Tue 9/21.
- Lauren: allocate GPU slot for throughput sweeps (120 reqs/min target) and add to ops-checklist.xlsx.
- Monica: prepare CS onboarding checklist and acceptance doc template for Samir to sign (we’ll use this as the formal acceptance).

If you can flag anything I missed, shout. I’ll proceed with the baseline run once we have access.

Rafael
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Connective.ai trial scope & ops next steps

Quick update on the infra items — I validated the preview runtime and can confirm we record cache events at the session level. Plan below:

- Instrumentation: expose a per-session cache_hit_rate metric (0-1) in the tracing payload; also add a small synthetic that emits cache-hit distribution for a 1k-session sample.
- Baseline runs: I’ll run the smoke baseline on the provided 250-token normalized convo and report: median latency, 95th-pct latency, avg tokens/request, and per-conversation cost (we’ll compute using both tokenized and model-internal token counts).
- Throughput sweeps: Lauren — please schedule the 1-hour throughput window Tue 09/21 10:00-11:00 PT; I’ll run 120 reqs/min sustained and log CPU/GPU utilization.

I attached an updated ops-checklist.xlsx with the GPU slot and test window. Rafael — once Samir confirms the bucket access I’ll kick off the baseline.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@connective.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Trial owners, acceptance template & 9/24 readout cadence

Samir — looping you in with the ops owners and a simple acceptance template so we can sign off quickly after the acceptance run. Attached: ops-checklist.xlsx (tasks + schedule) and trial-data-sample.csv (schema reference).

Acceptance template (summary):
- Acceptance criteria met: yes/no
- Quality: precision, recall (target >0.88)
- Performance: 95th-pct latency <= 300ms (target), median latency reported, throughput achieved
- Cost: per-conversation cost (target < $0.10) and per-1k-token equivalent
- Evidence links: baseline run artifacts, trace with cache_hit_rate samples, throughput logs

Proposed readout: Fri 9/24 10:00 PT — 30-minute slot for results + decision. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read one pager.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
